about: Flint (Recursive's 39.8B MoE, ~2.5B active; 49 layers, 256 experts top-6, 14 full-attention layers) Q4_K_M on one 12 GB card with every routed expert in system RAM and llama.cpp's MoE expert cache in VRAM: -ngl 99 with --n-cpu-moe 49 keeps attention, the shared expert and 131,072 tokens of f16 KV (two 65,536-token slots, --parallel 2) on the GPU and all routed experts in host RAM (--load-mode none reads them in rather than mmapping them, which makes host-to-GPU copies faster); --moe-cache-mib 2944 holds the hottest experts on the GPU (the adaptive cache serves ~45% of expert reads from VRAM on code), and --moe-cache-cpu-share 0.95 lets the CPU compute most cache misses instead of uploading them (1.0 freezes the cache). --fit off because the layout is set by hand. -b/-ub 4096 amortises the expert copies over PCIe during prefill (4.1x prefill over the defaults). f16 KV: q8_0 KV costs ~29% decode at 32k depth on this model. -t 6: RAM bandwidth saturates at 6 threads. Recursive's recommended sampling. Measured on one RTX 3060 12GB (PCIe 4.0 x16), i5-12500, 62 GiB RAM (57 GB/s measured read). Two slots of 64k rather than one of 128k: single-slot 128k passes a 120k-token needle test on a code haystack but recalls the lab's repetitive filler at ~87k tokens only 0-2 times in 3 (spec on or off, -ub 512, cache off, question first), while 43k and 65k recall 3/3.
